conflict_topics: who works the two days around the Hari Raya Puasa public holiday
religious observance (Hari Raya) versus prepaid family holiday
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers provide concrete, independent reasons (paid bookings, childcare closure, religious obligations) rather than abstract claims.
Several turns restate prior positions verbatim or near-verbatim (e.g., multiple "I can't cancel" and "I've done my bit" lines).
No proposed solution, manager decision, or third-party intervention appears in the transcript.
Conversation is consistent with the workplace setting and constraints (no relief staff, two required on duty).
evaluation.final_reason: No settlement was reached. All four staff stated they could not work the two contested days (e.g., Agent A: "I've already booked a family holiday, months ago." Agent B: "My kid's childcare is closed on those days." Agent D: "I need those days for Hari Raya." Agent B at the end: "Make that four of us. ... I have no choice."). No one offered an accepted trade, accommodation, or concrete arrangement to ensure two people would be on duty, so the substantive incompatibility remained unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A consistently refused to change: Turn 1 "I can't change mine..." and repeated in Turns 5, 9, 22.
Agent B consistently maintained inability to change due to childcare: Turn 2 and final Turn 28 "Make that four of us... I have no choice."
Agent C consistently invoked past coverage entitlement and demanded time off: Turn 3, Turn 17, Turn 21/23; no backdown observed.
Agent D consistently asserted the religious need to be off for Hari Raya and did not offer compromise: Turn 4, Turn 10, Turn 24, Turn 26.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: "I can't change mine. I've already booked a family holiday, months ago." Agent B: "I can't change either. My kid's childcare is closed on those days." (Two staff declare they cannot change; a potential staffing problem is set up but not yet contested.)

Agent C: "I want those days off as well. I've covered every holiday for two years." Agent D: "I need those days for Hari Raya." (Now four staff have expressed leave claims for two days that require two people on duty — clear substantive incompatibility emerges.)
Agent A: "I can't cancel it." Agent C: "And we all have our reasons." (Positions and reasons repeated; conflict about who will work remains unresolved.)

Agent D: "But this is the biggest holiday for us." Agent A: "...the whole family's trip is booked. I can't just cancel on them." (Reinforces incompatible claims: religious observance vs prepaid family holiday.)

Agent D describes specific Hari Raya activities: "The day before is for preparing... The second day is for visiting relatives." Agent A: expresses sympathy but remains unavailable. (No accommodation or solution proposed.)
Agent D: "But a holiday is not the same as Hari Raya." Agent A: "...flights and hotels are already paid for. I can't get the money back." (Conflicting weights of obligations restated; no resolution.)

Agent C: "I've worked every single holiday for two years so you all could have your leave." Agent D: "I've only been here a few months." (Fairness/entitlement dispute intensifies the incompatibility about who must work.)
Agent C: "It's someone else's turn." Agent D: "So it's their turn, then." (Positions on turn-taking remain contested; no agreement reached.)
Agent A repeats inability to cancel: "My trip is booked and paid for." Agent C reiterates turn-taking: "It is about whose turn it is." (Standoff continues with mutual insistence.)
Agent A: "I'm not available. The holiday is booked." Agent C: "But two people still have to work. And I've done my bit." (Practical need to staff shifts remains unmet; no one offers to cover.)

Agent D: "So that's two people who aren't working. We still need two people on duty. And I can't work on Hari Raya." Agent A: "Well, I can't work either." (At least three staff state they cannot work, creating an entrenched staffing impasse.)

Agent D: "So that's three of us who can't work." Agent B: "Make that four of us. My childcare is closed on both days. I have no choice." (All four staff confirm inability to work those days — complete, unresolved impasse.)

substantive_insights: Conflict arises from a scarcity problem: two required on duty vs four staff requesting leave.
Different types of obligations (religious observance, prepaid family travel, childcare) create competing, non-comparable claims.
A history of one person covering holidays (Agent C) produces fairness claims but no mechanism for enforcing rotation.
Because there is no established priority rule and no relief staff, individual constraints lead quickly to a collective impasse.
